heading: Stock Market Today Highlights: BSE Sensex gains 564 points; Nifty50 settles above 23,400 - The Times of India
paragraphs: Among the 30 Sensex firms, UltraTech Cement jumped 4.11 per cent. HCL Tech, Eternal, Titan, ITC and Tech Mahindra were also among the prominent winners.
Bharti Airtel, Power Grid, Infosys and Adani Ports were among the laggards.
Shares of Manika Plastech Ltd on Monday made a flat market debut, listing at par with the issue price of Rs 43. The stock listed at Rs 43 on both the BSE and NSE.

Further in the trade, it quoted at Rs 40.86, down 4.97 per cent from the issue price on the BSE. At the NSE, the stock declined 5 per cent to Rs 40.85. The company's market valuation stood at Rs 476.07 crore.
Market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty climbed in early trade on Monday amid cooling crude oil prices, fresh foreign fund inflows and a positive trend in Asian equities.
The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 448.32 points to 74,743.28 in early trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty was up 50.3 points to 23,396.70.
Among the 30 Sensex firms, UltraTech Cement, InterGlobe Aviation, Asian Paints, Sun Pharma, HCL Tech and Trent were the major winners.
Infosys, Adani Ports, Bharti Airtel and Power Grid were the laggards.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, tanked 2.25 per cent to USD 101.5 per barrel.
Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 599.54 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.
In Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi, Shanghai's SSE Composite index and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index were quoting in positive territory.

Indian shares were likely to open muted on Monday as elevated crude oil prices kept investors concerned about their impact on inflation and interest rates.
GIFT Nifty futures stood at 23,338 points at 7:49 am IST, indicating a flat start for the Nifty 50.

Asian shares edged higher on Monday, helped by gains in chipmakers as demand for artificial intelligence technology continued to support the sector. Oil prices eased as expectations of stronger Saudi supplies outweighed concerns over the latest Houthi attack.

Trading was relatively thin, with Japan's markets closed for the Silver Week holiday through Wednesday. The dollar was steady at 157 yen, while investors remained cautious about possible intervention by Japanese authorities to support the currency.
Japan's Nikkei was closed, although futures rose 0.5%. South Korea's tech-heavy index gained 1.1%, while MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.3%.

NSE IPO: Shareholders still retain significant stake despite tendering shares in offer-for-sale

NSE IPO: Most existing shareholders of the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) have continued to hold a substantial part of their stakes even after selling shares through the offer-for-sale (OFS) portion of the exchange's Rs 22,569-crore initial public offering (IPO).
Of the 20 institutional investors that participated in the OFS, nine were foreign institutional investors. These investors collectively owned 15.96 per cent of NSE before the IPO.

The other 11 participating institutions were domestic investors. This group included 10 public sector entities and ICICI Lombard General Insurance, with their combined holding standing at 20.86 per cent before the OFS.
